title: Ninety-four Jeunesse concerts and the flower parades
summary: He remembers concerts in top halls and parades in Holland and Nice.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: But when I see guys like Vic, Pete Brown, you know, and guys like that...and Doc Cheatham and all these things that were written by black people, plus Gershwin and others. And when I think of how that...I had an opportunity to play, incidentally, 94 concerts for the Jeunesse Musical / how successful it was. We had...we played nothing but top concert halls... that's not what they called it...they didn't call it a theater, either. But anyway, we played only the top places in every town. And with an entourage meeting us at the station. And
you know, I never ate so many bon-bons and drank hot coffee in my life.

And I remember one time we were playing in Holland for Lou van Rees and in Dumbosh. ...I don't know if you know where that is in Holland, they had this big parade for us, ten blocks long, and each of us was in a carriage, with the open thing, and they were throwing flowers all the way. But they did that, too, when I was there with Louis in '48 in Nice. On the boardwalk they had this parade of flowers. I was riding with Velma Middleton and Milton Mezzrow. What a combination! (Laughter).
